chapter: Sidemen, mixed bands, the Apollo and Lena Horne
title: Dizzy Gillespie on first trumpet and the Cincinnati mixed band
summary: Dizzy briefly played first trumpet in Barnet's band for a Cincinnati hotel job with Joe Guy; the local committee was curious, not hostile.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Dizzy was in your band very briefly, right?
Yeah. And you know what Dizzy played with me? Dizzy played first trumpet.
Oh, yeah? No, I didn't know that. I just knew he'd played for you.
Well, I had a job to go on the road, and I didn't have a trumpet section. You know, it was

scuffling time and we were going to play at the -- some hotel, the Netherlands Plaza or someplace in Cincinnati. So I got ahold of Dizzy, I said, "Hey, you want to make this trip?" He said, "Yeah, sure." I said, "Well, John, we need another trumpet player, too. You got anybody in mind?" He said, "How about Joe Guy?" I said, "Okay. I don't know him, but if you --," He said, "Yeah, he'll be fine." I said, "There's only one thing, John, you've got to play first trumpet." He said, "I'll play it." And he did. He did a heck of a job.
Wow. That was right after he left Calloway, right?
Yeah. Yeah. And that was a place where I -- you know, Cincinnati's pretty close to the jumping off place as far as that kind of stuff -- mixed bands are concerned.

The committee came over and they said -- the same curiosity that I had run into. Not antagonism, but like how can you -- how do you -- fine, how can you work like this? Is it all right? Is there any problem? I said, "No, I don't have any problems. Do you?" You know, it was more curiosity. This was what I was confronted with with this. I never in my life had a scene, you know, an out and out scene. The basic reaction seemed to me to be more curiosity, like how we could do this, rather than, "You dirty so and so, what are you trying to do?" I didn't run into any of that.
